correctness.rationale: The sample-size-one-through-four normalized drift polynomials have been expanded and checked. For 1<u<3 the weighted normalized drift is concave with positive endpoint; for u>3 it is positive throughout the interior. Neither permits a two-sided attracting interior root. For the size-two/size-five witness with 1<u<3/2, the exact factorization gives Q_q, whose unique interval minimum, endpoint signs, and two critical points yield an iff weight threshold and exactly two interior roots. The lower-root sign change proves asymptotic stability. The included checker reproduces symbolic identities and 999 exact rational signs; the proof, not finite numerics, covers all admissible parameters.

value.rationale: The central question in the originating paper is when heterogeneous learning can sustain miscoordination. Establishing the smallest maximum observation size is a natural, globally quantified structural boundary; the exact transition weight and full local phase portrait in its first realizable case make the statement directly usable for modeling observation heterogeneity. This is not a single unmotivated numerical example, an existing general sufficient theorem, or a mere change of notation.
